findings.explanation: The Lean statement applies List.reverse to the swapped list before ALOOKUP; the HOL4 statement uses ALOOKUP (MAP (λ(x,y). (y,x)) ls) x with no REVERSE. Both REV_ASSOCD and ALOOKUP return the first match, so the Lean statement returns the last match on the right-hand side and is false when a key occurs twice with different values. Example: ls = [(1,0),(2,0)], x = 0, d = 0. The left side is 1 and the Lean right side is 2 (the HOL4 right side is 1).
findings.repair:
theorem REV_ASSOCD_ALOOKUP {α : Type u} {β : Type v} :
    ∀ (ls : List (α × β)) (x : β) (d : α),
      REV_ASSOCD x ls d =
        match ALOOKUP (ls.map (fun (x, y) => (y, x))) x with
        | none => d
        | some y => y := by
  sorry
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSyntaxLib

example : ¬ (type_of% @Candle.REV_ASSOCD_ALOOKUP.{0,0}) := by
  intro h
  have h1 := @h Nat Nat [(1, 0), (2, 0)] 0 0
  simp [Candle.REV_ASSOCD, HOL.ALOOKUP] at h1
findings.hol4_check: (REV_ASSOCD 0n [(1n,0n);(2n,0n)] 0n = 1n) /\ ((case ALOOKUP (MAP (\(x,y). (y,x)) [(1n,0n);(2n,0n)]) 0n of NONE => 0n | SOME y => y) = 1n) /\ ((case ALOOKUP (REVERSE (MAP (\(x,y). (y,x)) [(1n,0n);(2n,0n)])) 0n of NONE => 0n | SOME y => y) = 2n)
